unit.why: A short miracle legend about the pre-Hasidic sage Maharam: during Kiddush Levana after Yom Kippur the clouds scatter at his word. It ends with source references.
unit.boundary_note: opening may be truncated (begins with '140 מהר"ם', possibly a running number or a continuation of the previous line)

stories.end_quote: וברך ברכת הלבנה בשמחה רבה עכ״ל
stories.summary_en: When clouds hid the moon as Maharam and his court stood to sanctify it after Yom Kippur, he cried 'how bold is the face of the firmament, Meir and his court are standing', and a wind scattered the clouds, so he blessed the moon in great joy.

tags.why: praises the wonder-working of a pre-Hasidic rabbinic authority, cited from earlier books
